skill.description: Guide for designing, scaffolding, validating, and packaging AI skills with concise SKILL.md instructions, progressive disclosure, reusable resources, and local helper scripts.
skill.summary: Create effective AI skills with structured guidance, templates, validation, and packaging helpers.
skill.author: AbdullahMalik17

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline filenames, and the word keys in YAML validation code. The review found no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent, but the helper scripts have local filesystem risks around unvalidated skill names and broad archive inclusion.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated skill names can escape the selected output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Validate skill_name against the documented hyphen-case rule, reject path separators and '..', and ensure the resolved output stays under the selected directory before writing files.

remediation.issue: Skill archives may include unintended local files.
remediation.suggestion: Add an allowlist or exclusion list for __pycache__, hidden files, virtual environments, archives, and credential-like filenames before writing the .skill file.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Controls Output Path
semantic_findings.description: scripts/init_skill.py combines the user-supplied output path with skill_name before creating directories and files. A name containing path separators or parent directory segments could write generated files outside the intended output folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code joins Path(path).resolve() with raw skill_name and then creates the directory. The CLI text states naming rules, but the script does not enforce them before filesystem writes.

semantic_findings.title: Packager Archives All Files Under Skill Directory
semantic_findings.description: scripts/package_skill.py walks every file beneath the provided skill directory and writes each one into the archive. Without exclusions, hidden files, caches, or local secrets placed in the skill folder could be shared unintentionally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The archive loop uses rglob over all files and writes each result without filtering. This is a clear packaging behavior, though impact depends on what files the user has placed in the skill directory.

content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills requires clear structure, concise context, and safe packaging. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, scaffolding, writing, validating, and packaging skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md structure and frontmatter fields.
Guides decisions about scripts, references, and assets for reusable workflows.
Scaffolds a new skill folder with starter files and resource directories.
Validates skill frontmatter, naming rules, and description constraints.
Packages a validated skill folder into a distributable .skill archive.
Provides reference patterns for workflow design and output examples.
limitations: It does not publish skills to any marketplace or registry.
Generated templates require user editing before they are useful.
Local scripts require Python and the expected dependencies to be installed.
The packager does not automatically filter every unintended file type.

use_cases.title: Design a New Skill
use_cases.description: Plan triggers, workflows, and reusable resources for a new AI skill before writing files.

use_cases.title: Convert Team Process Notes
use_cases.description: Turn internal procedures into concise skill instructions with supporting references and examples.

use_cases.title: Validate and Package a Skill
use_cases.description: Check frontmatter and create a distributable .skill archive after implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for defining scope and structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a skill for [task]. Ask the minimum questions needed, then propose the SKILL.md structure and required resources.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a Skill Folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for creating starter files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to initialize a new [skill-name] skill under [path]. Then explain which generated files I should edit or delete.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for revising quality and trigger behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing skill for trigger clarity, progressive disclosure, resource organization, and packaging readiness. Suggest concrete edits before packaging.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Domain Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for complex skills with many resources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for a multi-domain skill with scripts, references, assets, validation steps, packaging checks, and review criteria.

output_examples.input: I need a skill for monthly metrics analysis.
output_examples.output: A concise skill plan with trigger wording, workflow sections, and a short list of scripts and reference files.
A local skill folder with SKILL.md, example resources, and next editing steps for replacing placeholders.
A validation result followed by an archive path, or clear fixes when validation fails.

best_practices: Start from real user requests before writing the skill body.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move large supporting detail into references.
Test bundled scripts with representative inputs before packaging.
anti_patterns: Adding process documents that do not help the agent perform the task.
Leaving generated placeholder files in the final package.
Using broad descriptions that cause the skill to trigger too often.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI skills with clear triggers, concise instructions, reusable resources, validation, and packaging.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The initializer can create a local skill folder, SKILL.md, and example resource directories.

faq.question: Can it update an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for reviewing triggers, resource structure, and iterative improvements.

faq.question: Does it validate every security concern?
faq.answer: No. It checks basic structure, but users must review scripts, assets, and packaged files separately.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it publish the skill?
faq.answer: No. It creates a local .skill archive that a user can share through a separate process.
